subject: Question about RMA and custom CDF

messages.author: 239f8e443869b2fe
messages.subject: Question about RMA and custom CDF
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering whether aroma-affymetrix package supports the use of custom CDF.

http://brainarray.mbni.med.umich.edu/Brainarray/Database/CustomCDF/genomic_curated_CDF.asp

If yes, should I use the custom CDF the same way as CDF from Affy.

In addition, if I want to use RMA method to do background correction, normalization and summarization of gene expression from probe data, can I just use the following code?

bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)

csBC <- process(bc)

qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC)

csN <- process(qn)
plm <- RmaPlm(csN)

Thanks a lot.

Yiwen Chen

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Question about RMA and custom CDF
parts:
Hi Yiwen.

Indeed, aroma.affymetrix supports custom CDF files.

For example (Human Exon 1.0 ST array with the Brainarray RefSeq custom
CDF):
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/hsex10stv2-hs-refseq

As another example, say you were interested in the Human Gene 1.0 ST
array and the ENTREZG custom CDF. Here is what you could do:

1. Download the ZIP file from the rightmost link of the Brainarray
custom CDF page (i.e. not the R *package* but the zip file containing
the CDF, probe_tab, map, etc.)

from here:
http://brainarray.mbni.med.umich.edu/Brainarray/Database/CustomCDF/12.0.0/entrezg.asp

download:
http://brainarray.mbni.med.umich.edu/Brainarray/Database/CustomCDF/12.0.0/entrezg.download/HuGene10stv1_Hs_ENTREZG_12.0.0.zip

2. Unzip that file and you will see a text-formatted CDF file.

3. Convert that file into binary using convertCdf() from the
'affxparser' package.

4. Put the binary CDF file in your annotationData/chipTypes directory
and for RMA processing, analyze as you mention below.

Cheers,
Mark
